What's inside — all 14 files

Spreadsheets (Excel / Google Sheets):

  1. Pricing Calculator — enter turf area, obstacle level, service type, and frequency; get a per-visit price with trim time and unload time counted, plus monthly and full-season estimates and a minimum stop price you can't quote under.
  2. Recurring Client & Route Tracker — every client by service day, with a route-day board showing revenue per hour for each day and a density tab that puts a number on what drive time is costing you. This is the workbook that shows you which route day is a truck payment in disguise.
  3. Income & Expense Tracker — a monthly P&L with this trade's categories built in: fuel, blades and parts, equipment repair, fertilizer, dump fees.
  4. Job Costing Sheet — per-visit labor, fuel, materials, and equipment reserve, so you find the long-standing clients whose price stopped working three years ago.

Documents (editable Word / Google Docs):

  1. Residential Lawn Care Service Agreement — scope, schedule, and terms in writing before the first cut.
  2. Commercial Landscape Maintenance Contract — for HOAs and commercial properties, where a handshake stops being enough.
  3. Client Intake Form — every detail you need before the first visit, asked once instead of texted forever.
  4. Quote / Estimate Template — a professional quote that goes out the same day the call comes in.
  5. Invoice Template — clean, clear, and easier to pay than to ignore.
  6. Client Welcome Packet — policies, how to reach you, and the review ask, delivered up front.
  7. Policies & Letters — weather and scheduling policy, cancellation/skip/no-access policy, price-increase letter, and review-request and complaint scripts.
  8. Property Condition Acknowledgment & Damage Waiver — the two calls that damage this business fastest are a cut irrigation head and a severed invisible-fence wire. This is the walkthrough that makes marking the client's job, the waiver that covers thrown objects and trimmer contact, and the addendum for when a client insists you scalp the lawn in July.

Checklists:

  1. Seasonal Service Schedule & Checklists — the standard mowing visit, spring cleanup, fertilization and treatment (including the licensing gate most new operators don't know about), aeration and overseeding, and fall cleanup and winterization.
  2. Startup Checklist — licensing, insurance, equipment with realistic 2026 budgets, applicator licensing before you sell any treatment, and how to build a dense route instead of a scattered one.

Who it's for — and who it's not for

For you if: you're starting a lawn care or landscape maintenance business — or you've been running one on memory, texts, and a notebook. Solo operators and small crews. If you've never worked out what a stop actually earns you after drive time, start here.

Not for you if: you're buying into a franchise (they hand you their systems), you need jurisdiction-specific legal documents drafted for your state (that's an attorney, and worth it), or you're looking for agronomy training. This is paperwork and pricing infrastructure — it won't teach you turf science, it makes the business side work.

FAQ

Can I edit the templates? Yes — every file is fully editable. Replace the placeholders with your business name, adjust the terms and the rates, and use them as your own.

Are these legal documents? No. They're business templates written from operating experience, and they're a far better starting point than a blank page. Contract law varies by state, so have a local attorney review anything you'll rely on — particularly the waiver.

Will the pricing calculator work in my market? The defaults are sane 2026 US suburban starting points, and every rate is a yellow cell you can change: target hourly rate, mowing production rates, obstacle factors, frequency multipliers, and your mowing weeks per season. Southern operators mow forty weeks; northern operators mow twenty-six. Set yours.

Does it handle biweekly clients? Yes — and it prices them higher per visit, not lower. Double the growth and double the mess for the same drive is a cost, not a discount, and most new operators get that backwards.

Do I need special software? No. Word and Excel work, and so do the free Google and Apple equivalents.

Templates are starting points, not legal advice. Have a local attorney review contracts before use.
